title: Apply Operations to Make String Empty
summary: Given a string s , repeatedly remove the first occurrence of each alphabet character from 'a' to 'z' until s becomes empty.
statement: Given a string s , repeatedly remove the first occurrence of each alphabet character from 'a' to 'z' until s becomes empty. Return the string s right before the final removal. For example, starting with "aabcbbca", the process yields "abbca", then "ba", and finally an empty string, so the answer is "ba".
constraints: s is a nonempty lowercase string.
Each round removes the first remaining occurrence of every character that is still present.
Return the exact remaining string immediately before the final round, preserving its order.
hints: A character survives into the final nonempty round exactly when its total frequency is globally maximal.
Keep the last occurrence of every maximum-frequency character in original position order.
Count frequencies, record last indices, and emit positions that are both last and have maximum count.
After maximum-1 rounds only maximum-frequency characters remain once each, specifically at their original last occurrences; all others were exhausted earlier.
editorial: After maximum-1 rounds only maximum-frequency characters remain once each, specifically at their original last occurrences; all others were exhausted earlier.

tests.explanation: After two rounds the remaining string is ba; the third round removes both characters.
Every character occurs once, so the original string is the state immediately before the only round.
